# 04. Vocabulary

Lexicon version 0.1.0.

## How words are made / 造詞方式

1. Every concept (from [Concepticon](https://concepticon.clld.org), plus a few of our own) gets a frequency: how often it is used across English, Spanish, German, Chinese and Japanese.
2. Huffman coding turns frequencies into word lengths: frequent concepts get 1 syllable, rarer ones 2 or 3.
3. Among words of the same length, syllables with fewer letters go to more frequent concepts, and neighbouring syllables share no sound, so frequent words don't sound alike.
4. 10% of the two-syllable words are kept free for words added later (see [00 Introduction](00-introduction.md#versions--版本)).

Some concepts don't get a word of their own:

- **Pronouns**: 33 pronoun concepts (ME, MY, HIS, WE TWO …) use one of the 7 pronouns.
- **Compounds**: concepts made of existing concepts are said with those words, head first: COCONUT TREE → TREE COCONUT (*ihë könah*).

## Numbers / 數字

| --- | --- |
| Concepts | 4,108 |
| With their own word | 3,752 |
| Said with another concept's word (pronouns) | 25 |
| Said with existing words (compounds) | 331 |
| Words with 1 / 2 / 3 syllables | 376 / 2,833 / 543 |
| Average word, weighted by use | 1.16 syllables, 2.32 letters |
| Free slots for new words | 315 with 2 syllables, 157 with 3 syllables |

## Full list / 完整詞表

[lexicon/0.1.0.tsv](../lexicon/0.1.0.tsv): every concept with its word, syllables, the spelling with zero consonants (`cvc`) and IPA. `rank` orders the words from most to least frequent. The frequencies themselves are not published (see [ATTRIBUTION.md](../ATTRIBUTION.md)).
